'''Helen Fay Dowker''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|aʊ|k|ər}}; born 9 September 1965) is a British physicist who is a current professor of [[theoretical physics]] at [[Imperial College London]].<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dowker |first1=Fay |author-link=Fay Dowker |last2=Gauntlett |first2=Jerome P. |last3=Kastor |first3=David A. |last4=Traschen |first4=Jennie|author4-link= Jennie Traschen |year= 1994 |title=Pair creation of dilaton black holes |journal=[[Physical Review D]] |volume=49 |issue=6 |pages=2909–2917 |arxiv=hep-th/9309075 |bibcode=1994PhRvD..49.2909D |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.49.2909|pmid=10017283 |s2cid=15303024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dowker |first1=Fay |author-link=Fay Dowker |last2=Gauntlett |first2=Jerome P. |author3-link=Steven Giddings|last3=Giddings |first3=Steven B. |last4=Horowitz |first4=Gary T. |year= 1994 |title=Pair creation of extremal black holes and Kaluza-Klein monopoles |journal=[[Physical Review D]] |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=2662–2679 |arxiv=hep-th/9312172 |bibcode=1994PhRvD..50.2662D |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.50.2662|pmid=10017899 |s2cid=7270273 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dowker |first1=Fay |author-link=Fay Dowker |last2=Gauntlett |first2=Jerome P. |last3=Gibbons |first3=Gary W. |last4=Horowitz |first4=Gary T. |year= 1995 |title=Decay of magnetic fields in Kaluza-Klein theory |journal=[[Physical Review D]] |volume=52 |issue=12 |pages=6929–6940 |arxiv=hep-th/9507143 |bibcode=1995PhRvD..52.6929D |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.52.6929|pmid=10019234 |s2cid=16857664 }}</ref><ref name="imdb">{{IMDb name |3217574 |Fay Dowker}}</ref>

==Education==
Dowker attended [[Manchester High School for Girls]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 November 2019 |title=A Brief History of Time at Manchester High |url=https://jlifemagazine.co.uk/news-manchester/brief-history-of-time-at-manchester-high |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=JLife Magazine |language=en-GB}}</ref> As a student, she was interested in [[wormholes]] and [[quantum cosmology]]. Having studied the [[Mathematical Tripos]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], Dowker was awarded the [[Tyson Medal]] in 1987 and completed her Doctor of Philosophy for research on [[spacetime]] [[wormhole]]s supervised by [[Stephen Hawking]]<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=156314}}</ref><ref name="dowkerphd" /> in 1990.<ref name="dowkerphd"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hawking.org.uk/index.php/about-stephen/stephenatcambridge/formerstudents |title=Former Students |website=hawking.org.uk |publisher=Stephen Hawking |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090228131018/http://www.hawking.org.uk/index.php/about-stephen/stephenatcambridge/formerstudents |archive-date=2009-02-28 }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Dowker completed [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Fermilab]], at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and also the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>[http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/people/f.dowker Dowker, Fay] Page at Imperial College London</ref><ref>[http://web.ukonline.co.uk/f.dowker/ Dowker, Fay] Personal webpage (last updated 2003) {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060409154638/http://web.ukonline.co.uk/f.dowker/ |date=9 April 2006 }}</ref>

Until 2003, Dowker was a lecturer at [[Queen Mary University of London]].<ref>[https://www.imperial.ac.uk/theoretical-physics/about-us/history/ History] Theoretical Physics Group, Imperial College London</ref>

She is currently a professor of Theoretical Physics and a member of the Theoretical Physics Group at [[Imperial College London]] and a Visiting Fellow at the [[Perimeter Institute]].<ref>[https://perimeterinstitute.ca/people/fay-dowker Fay Dowker, Perimeter Institute]</ref> She conducts research in a number of areas of theoretical physics including [[quantum gravity]] and [[Causal Sets|causal set theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dowker |first=Fay |author-link=Fay Dowker |year=2013 |title=Introduction to causal sets and their phenomenology |journal=[[General Relativity and Gravitation]] |volume=45 |issue=9 |pages=1651–1667 |bibcode=2013GReGr..45.1651D |doi=10.1007/s10714-013-1569-y|s2cid=119465367 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dowker |first1=Fay |author-link=Fay Dowker |last2=Glaser |first2=Lisa |year=2013 |title=Causal set d'Alembertians for various dimensions |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=30 |issue=19 |article-number=195016 |arxiv=1305.2588 |bibcode=2013CQGra..30s5016D |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/30/19/195016|s2cid=119181630 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Afshordi |first1=Niayesh |last2=Buck |first2=Michel |last3=Dowker |first3=Fay |author-link3=Fay Dowker |last4=Rideout |first4=David |last5=Sorkin |first5=Rafael D. |author-link5=Rafael Sorkin |last6=Yazdi |first6=Yasaman K. |year=2012 |title=A ground state for the causal diamond in 2 dimensions |journal=[[Journal of High Energy Physics]] |volume=2012 |issue=10 |page=88 |arxiv=1207.7101 |bibcode=2012JHEP...10..088A |doi=10.1007/JHEP10(2012)088|s2cid=119182974 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dowker is the daughter of physicist Stuart Dowker, who worked at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518091941/http://www.theory.physics.manchester.ac.uk/~dowker/|archive-date=18 May 2017|url=http://www.theory.physics.manchester.ac.uk/~dowker/|publisher=University of Manchester|author=Anon|year=2015|title=Stuart Dowker}}</ref><ref name=DowkerElizalde2012>{{cite journal|last1=Dowker|first1=Fay|last2=Elizalde|first2=Emilio|last3=Kirsten|first3=Klaus|title=Applications of zeta functions and other spectral functions in mathematics and physics: a special issue in honour of Stuart Dowker's 75th birthday|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=45|issue=37|year=2012|article-number=370301|issn=1751-8113|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/45/37/370301|bibcode=2012JPhA...45a0101D|doi-access=}}</ref> She was interviewed by [[Jim Al-Khalili]] for ''[[The Life Scientific]]'' in 2017.<ref name=tls/>

She delivered the eulogy at [[Stephen Hawking]]'s funeral, describing him as her "teacher, mentor and friend" and asserting that "his influence and legacy will live forever."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cambridgeshire-43582950|work=[[BBC News]]|title=Prof Stephen Hawking funeral: Legacy 'will live forever'|date=31 March 2018}}</ref>
